newsitem.title: JAPAN: Showa Shell to hasten cost-cutting efforts.
newsitem.headline: Showa Shell to hasten cost-cutting efforts.

text.p: Oil company Showa Shell Sekiyu KK said on Friday it would speed up plans to slash distribution costs in response to a deteriorating market environment.
The firm said it would aim to trim 13 billion yen from its distribution costs by 2000 compared to 1995, four years earlier than originally scheduled.
The efforts to cut distribution costs are part of a plan Showa Shell unveiled earlier this year aimed at improving profits by 40 billion yen by the year 2000.
Showa Shell, an oil refiner and distributor, is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
A company spokesman said Showa Shell plans to accelerate cost cutting in distribution by increasing oil product swapping arrangements with other refiners.
Possible partners in swap arrangements for high-quality gasoline would be Tonen Corp Cosmo Oil Co Ltd 5007 T and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, he said.
Japanese oil companies have been battling to cut costs as earnings from gasoline sales have plummeted in the past two years due to tumbling retail prices.
